title: Changing Gait Without Stumbling: Phase Tables for Walk, Trot, Pace and Bound, Turning One Into Another at a Bounded Rate, and a Switch With a Gap

questions.question: What is a gait, as the controller sees it?
options: A table of phase offsets, one for each leg
A list of foot positions, one for each instant
A speed and a step length
A duty and a period, the same for every leg
questions.explanation: The legs share one clock, and each is ahead of it by its own fraction of a cycle. A walk, a trot, a pace and a bound differ only in those four fractions.

questions.question: Why is a phase difference wrapped before it is limited?
options: Because a phase above 1 makes the leg skip a step
So that all four legs change by the same amount
0.95 and 0.05 are 0.1 apart on the circle, not 0.9
Because the rate limit only works on positive numbers
questions.explanation: A phase is a place on a circle. Without the wrap an offset at 0.95 with a target of 0.05 would go back by 0.9 when the target is 0.1 ahead.

questions.question: The abrupt change jumped a leg's phase by:
options: 0.0002 of a cycle in one tick
0.5 of a cycle, a whole stance
Nothing: the offsets are only read at touchdown
0.250 of a cycle in one tick
questions.explanation: A quarter of a cycle in one tick tells a foot in stance that it is in swing. At a bounded rate the same change was spread over 1.25 s.

questions.question: A speed hovering at 0.5 m/s flapped how many times with one switch speed?
options: 0 times
400 times, once a reading
Twice: once up and once down
questions.explanation: With one threshold every reading that crosses it changes the gait: 175 of 400. With a gap between the speed to go up and the speed to come back down it did not flap at all.

questions.question: Why does the count of feet down not show the danger of an abrupt change?
options: The count is only taken once a cycle
The abrupt change left fewer feet down, but only for a tick
The bounded change left fewer feet down than the abrupt one
Both changes kept 2 or more feet down; the harm is the phase jump
questions.explanation: Counting feet says both are fine. The danger is what a single leg is asked to do: follow a phase that jumps.

questions.question: What is held fixed in this lesson?
options: The rate at which the offsets move
The duty and period during a change
The four tables of offsets
The gap between the two switch speeds
questions.explanation: Only the offsets were moved. A real change of gait usually changes the duty and the period as well, and they would be eased the same way.
